cards.prompt: Minimum components of a mammography unit under MQSA?
cards.answer: X-ray generator, x-ray control, tube housing assembly, beam-limiting device, and supporting structures.

cards.prompt: May general-purpose x-ray equipment with mammography attachments be used for mammography?
cards.answer: No. MQSA prohibits general-purpose or specially modified non-mammography systems.

cards.prompt: Order along the beam after the tube housing?
cards.answer: Beam-limiting device → compression paddle → breast → breast support/image receptor.

cards.prompt: What is bremsstrahlung?
cards.answer: X-rays produced when electrons decelerate in the anode (braking radiation).

cards.prompt: What are characteristic x-rays?
cards.answer: Photons emitted when an inner-shell vacancy in an anode atom is filled; energies identify the element.

cards.prompt: How is maximum photon energy related to tube voltage?
cards.answer: E_max equals the electron energy from the accelerating voltage (e.g., 100 kV → 100 keV max).

cards.prompt: Do lower- or higher-energy x-rays generally provide better subject contrast?
cards.answer: Lower-energy x-rays generally provide better contrast; higher-energy photons penetrate more.

cards.prompt: Why is soft-tissue contrast difficult on radiographs?
cards.answer: Different soft tissues absorb x-rays very similarly.

cards.prompt: Maximum flat-paddle deflection from parallel under compression?
Why press the breast between plates (NCI)?
cards.answer: Pressing helps get a better x-ray picture of the inside of the breast.

cards.prompt: MQSA magnification factor range that must be available?
cards.answer: At least one value between 1.4 and 2.0.

cards.prompt: Grid requirement for magnification systems?
cards.answer: Must be able to operate with the grid removed.

cards.prompt: What does SID stand for?
cards.answer: Source-to-image-receptor distance.

cards.prompt: Examples of mammographic modalities in MQSA?
cards.answer: Screen-film, full-field digital mammography (FFDM), and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT).

cards.prompt: How does DBT create a 3D picture (NCI)?
cards.answer: Takes multiple thin-slice pictures across the breast; software assembles them into a 3D picture.

cards.prompt: Does DBT also create 2D images?
cards.answer: Yes. NCI states DBT also creates 2D images like standard mammography.

cards.prompt: Is DBT proven to reduce breast-cancer deaths more than standard mammography alone?
cards.answer: Not established yet; NCI notes this is still being studied (e.g., TMIST).

cards.prompt: Acquisition workstation vs interpretation workstation?
cards.answer: Acquisition: technologist checks completeness/quality. Interpretation: physician diagnostic review.

cards.prompt: Where do detailed digital/DBT QC procedures live for many facilities?
cards.answer: In the image receptor manufacturer's program / commonly the ACR Digital Mammography QC Manual (link-only).

cards.prompt: After AEC, what technique factors must the system display?
cards.answer: Actual kVp and mAs used (and target/focal spot when algorithm-selected).

cards.prompt: Must manual selection of mAs (or mA/time) be available?
cards.answer: Yes.

cards.prompt: Why is diagnostic mammography dose higher than screening (NCI)?
cards.answer: Diagnostic exams require images from more angles.

cards.prompt: What must be indicated before exposure regarding the tube?
cards.answer: Selected focal spot and target material.

cards.prompt: Three technique changes typical of geometric magnification?
cards.answer: Increased OID/air gap, grid removed, small focal spot (with factor 1.4–2.0 available).

cards.prompt: List the eight clinical image review attributes.
cards.answer: Positioning, compression, exposure level, contrast, sharpness, noise, artifacts, examination identification.

cards.prompt: Must clinical images keep meeting accreditation quality standards between reviews?
cards.answer: Yes. Certified facilities must continue to comply with their AB's clinical image quality standards.

cards.prompt: What does ALARA stand for, and what are the three measures?
cards.answer: As low as reasonably achievable; time, distance, and shielding.

cards.prompt: What is the LNT model (NRC)?
cards.answer: Linear no-threshold: any increase in dose is assumed to increase cancer risk; used conservatively for protection estimates.

cards.prompt: How does NCI describe the x-ray dose level of mammography?
cards.answer: Low-dose x-rays.

cards.prompt: Primary cellular target of ionizing radiation damage discussed in OpenStax?
cards.answer: DNA molecules.

cards.prompt: Define the gray.
cards.answer: 1 Gy = 1 J/kg absorbed dose (= 100 rad).

history.note: Touches dose, thresholds, or device-specific practice; keep out of verified pools until qualified review.

cards.prompt: CDC clinic example of shielding for the technologist?
cards.answer: Going behind a barrier while making the x-ray exposure.

cards.prompt: MQSA phantom average glandular dose limit (single CC of standard-breast phantom)?
cards.answer: Must not exceed 3.0 mGy (0.3 rad) per exposure.

history.note: Touches dose, thresholds, or device-specific practice; keep out of verified pools until qualified review.

cards.prompt: MQSA standard breast definition used with phantom dose?
cards.answer: 4.2 cm compressed; 50% glandular / 50% adipose.
